issues.detail: The Greek 'εν ταις αγαπαις υμων' refers to 'in your loves' (plural), but the Vietnamese translates it as 'trong bữa tiệc yêu thương' (in the feast/party of love). The source text does not specify a 'feast' or 'party'.
The Greek 'συνευωχουμενοι' (rejoicing together) is translated as 'dự tiệc cùng nhau' (attending the party together), which carries the 'feast' connotation not present in the original.

The Greek 'εαυτους ποιμαινοντες' is a present active participle meaning 'pasturing themselves'. The Vietnamese 'chỉ nuôi chính mình' (only feeding/raising themselves) loses the specific imagery of 'pasturing/herding'.

The Greek 'poimainontes' (shepherding) is translated as 'chỉ nuôi chính mình' (only feeding themselves). The Vietnamese translation shifts the sense from 'shepherding/feeding others' to 'self-feeding', which distorts the intended meaning of the verb.
